letters.title: FDIC AG29 BSA and sanctions (PPSI)
letters.headline: FDIC AG29 PPSI BSA and sanctions comment
letters.h1: FDIC AG29 comment: a shared, reproducible control-posture record for PPSI supervision
letters.description: FDIC AG29 BSA and sanctions standards for PPSIs: one reproducible control-posture record for the FDIC and FinCEN to reason over. Six recommendations.
letters.thesis: The FDIC's supervision-and-coordination layer over a PPSI AML and sanctions program works only when the FDIC and FinCEN read the same measured control posture of one operator.
letters.gaps: Gaps: the effective-program disposition is left attestation-shaped; nothing keys the FDIC-to-FinCEN consultation to a shared, reproducible control-posture record.

recommendations.ask: Observable effective-program criteria
recommendations.text: Observable effective-program criteria (Question 1; Section 350.201). Rest the effective-program disposition on observable, reproducible indicators drawn from the FinCEN program requirements, not attestation alone, so a program is not treated as effective merely because policies or attestations exist. Prevents the disposition, which by the rule's terms shields a qualifying PPSI from AML/CFT enforcement, from becoming a paper-program safe harbor.

recommendations.ask: A shared control-posture record
recommendations.text: A shared control-posture record (Question 4; Section 350.202(b)(1)). Make a reproducible control-posture record a standing component of the FDIC-to-FinCEN notice package, so both agencies reason over the same measured object rather than reconstructing two records inside the notice window.

recommendations.ask: Thresholds keyed to posture
recommendations.text: Thresholds keyed to posture (Questions 2 and 3; Sections 350.200 and 350.202). Pair any outstanding-issuance-value threshold or PPSI-requested consultation option with a control-posture trigger keyed to the same record, and account for a GENIUS Act section 6(b) suspension or revocation premised in part on AML/CFT deficiencies.

recommendations.ask: Operational test of block, freeze, and reject capability
recommendations.text: Operational test of block, freeze, and reject capability (Section 350.6(d); Section IV.C). Require examination evidence that the sanctions capability works across both primary and secondary channels, with examination intensity scaled to measured holder concentration, rather than inferring it from the parent program or from the presence of on-chain functions.

recommendations.ask: An accountable line for parent-program reliance
recommendations.text: An accountable line for parent-program reliance (Question 1; Section 350.6(d)). Where a PPSI leverages its parent institution's program, confirm that one identifiable accountable line holds both the PPSI-specific control-posture information and the authority to act on it, so delegation does not diffuse responsibility.

recommendations.ask: Coverage across holding-location obligor changes
recommendations.text: Coverage across holding-location obligor changes (Question 1; Sections 350.201, 350.202, and 350.6(d)). Where a single tokenized instrument changes its obligor and applicable regime based on holding location, confirm that AML and sanctions coverage follows the instrument across the transition, treating the boundary crossing as a monitored event with continuity of identity and lawful-order controls.

letters.title: SEC Draft Strategic Plan (first SEC comment)
letters.headline: SEC DSP-3 Draft Strategic Plan comment
letters.h1: SEC DSP-3 comment: a measured, reproducible decentralization standard for the digital-asset regulatory foundation
letters.description: SEC Draft Strategic Plan FY 2026 to 2030 (File Number DSP-3): the plan's digital-asset objectives turn on a measurement capability it does not yet name.
letters.thesis: Where the plan's digital-asset objectives turn on whether a system is decentralized, decentralization must be measured against a reproducible standard the plan does not yet name.
letters.gaps: Gaps: naive holder lists inflate measured concentration 2.3x median (up to ~18x); launch allocation does not predict where control settles (r = 0.09).

recommendations.ask: Name reproducible measurement as the foundation capability
recommendations.text: Name reproducible measurement as the foundation capability (Objective 1.1). Name independent, reproducible measurement of digital-asset concentration and control as the capability the regulatory foundation rests on, so that any threshold the Commission later adopts rests on a method an outside party can reproduce from public on-chain data.

recommendations.ask: Frame oversight at the operator level, not the token level alone
recommendations.text: Frame oversight at the operator level, not the token level alone (Objective 1.1; custody, trading, and staking). Structural risk frequently concentrates at the operator rather than the token: the operator scoring highest on regulatory intensity experienced a 10 to 13 percent depeg during the March 2023 stress while a lower-scoring operator held its peg, and a single transfer agent serves all three documented tokenization strategies. Assess an operator across its full portfolio alongside token-level classification.

recommendations.ask: Measure decentralization wherever a boundary or jurisdictional determination turns on it
recommendations.text: Measure decentralization wherever a boundary or jurisdictional determination turns on it (Objective 1.1; boundaries of securities law and jurisdiction). Where the securities-law boundary or the SEC-CFTC allocation rests on the degree of a system's decentralization, measure that degree from current on-chain state, supported by indicators of current concentration and realized voting control, rather than inferring it from holder counts or disclosed allocations.

recommendations.ask: Build reproducible on-chain instruments into advanced analytics
recommendations.text: Build reproducible on-chain instruments into advanced analytics (Objective 3.2). Two dollar stablecoins on the same chain carried top-100 holder concentrations roughly five times apart in a single snapshot; reproducible concentration and control instruments, developed on public data, are adaptable to the registered products the Commission reviews. The offer is method transfer, not findings about registered products.

letters.title: OCC AF55 BSA and sanctions (PPSI)
letters.headline: OCC AF55 PPSI BSA and sanctions comment
letters.h1: OCC AF55 comment: one measured control posture, extended to reserve assets, entity types, and OCC-FDIC alignment
letters.description: OCC AF55 BSA and sanctions standards for PPSIs: one control-posture record for the OCC and FinCEN, extended to reserve assets. Eight recommendations.
letters.agency_long: Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC)
letters.thesis: Supervising a PPSI AML and sanctions program works only when the OCC and FinCEN read the same measured control posture of one operator, and the OCC and FDIC rules align.
letters.gaps: Gaps: the effective-program disposition is attestation-shaped; nothing keys the OCC-to-FinCEN consultation to a shared control-posture record; the OCC and FDIC consultation thresholds diverge (assets against outstanding issuance value), inviting arbitrage.

recommendations.ask: Observable effective-program criteria
recommendations.text: Observable effective-program criteria (Question 8; proposed Section 19.262). Rest the effective-program disposition on observable, reproducible indicators drawn from the FinCEN program requirements, not attestation alone, so a program is not treated as effective merely because policies or attestations exist. Prevents the disposition from becoming a paper-program safe harbor.

recommendations.ask: A shared control-posture record
recommendations.text: A shared control-posture record (Question 10; proposed Section 19.261(b)). Make a reproducible control-posture record a standing component of the OCC-to-FinCEN advance-notice package, so both agencies reason over the same measured object rather than reconstructing two records inside the notice window.

recommendations.ask: Thresholds keyed to posture
recommendations.text: Thresholds keyed to posture (Questions 8 and 9; proposed Sections 19.260 and 19.261). Pair any asset threshold or PPSI-requested consultation option with a control-posture trigger keyed to the same record, and account for a revocation of approval to issue premised in part on AML/CFT deficiencies.

recommendations.ask: Operational test of block, freeze, and reject capability
recommendations.text: Operational test of block, freeze, and reject capability (proposed Section 15.13(c)). Confirm by examination evidence that the sanctions capability works across both primary and secondary channels, with examination intensity scaled to measured holder concentration, rather than inferring it from the parent program or from the presence of on-chain functions.

recommendations.ask: An accountable line and a uniform standard across entity types
recommendations.text: An accountable line and a uniform standard across entity types (Questions 1 and 2; proposed Section 15.13(c)). Confirm that one identifiable accountable line holds both the control-posture information and the authority to act, and that the measured standard is uniform across entity types (national trust banks, bank affiliates, and non-bank issuers), addressing the overlap with part 21.

recommendations.ask: Coverage across holding-location obligor changes
recommendations.text: Coverage across holding-location obligor changes (proposed Sections 15.13(c), 19.261, and 19.262). Where a single tokenized instrument changes its obligor and applicable regime based on holding location, confirm that AML and sanctions coverage follows the instrument across the transition, treating the boundary crossing as a monitored event with continuity of identity and lawful-order controls, and with OCC-FinCEN consultation so the unexamined leg is not a blind spot.

recommendations.ask: Alignment with the parallel FDIC rule
recommendations.text: Alignment with the parallel FDIC rule (Question 6; proposed Sections 15.13(c), 19.261, 19.262, and 4.19). Align the OCC and FDIC supervision, consultation, and disclosure provisions on a common measured object, and reconcile the divergent consultation thresholds: 10 billion dollars in assets at the OCC (Question 9) against 10 billion dollars in outstanding issuance value at the FDIC (AG29 Question 3). This is the signature contribution of a commenter present on both dockets; an unreconciled divergence invites regulatory arbitrage.

recommendations.ask: Reserve-asset security and holder monetization keyed to measured concentration
recommendations.text: Reserve-asset security and holder monetization keyed to measured concentration (Questions 3, 4, and 5; proposed Sections 15.11 and 15.13). Treat reserve-asset identifiability, eligible-institution safeguards keyed to measured reserve-custody concentration, and a holder-monetization backstop keyed to measured secondary-market concentration as observable controls, and support the OCC direct-redemption option triggered on observable monetization-failure indicators.

letters.title: FinCEN AB74 PPSI customer identification program
letters.headline: FinCEN AB74 PPSI customer identification program comment
letters.h1: FinCEN AB74 comment: codify the account boundary the footnote states, and count the population the rule actually reaches
letters.description: FinCEN AB74 PPSI CIP: codify the account boundary that footnote 57 leaves in the preamble and count the population the rule reaches. Eight recommendations.
letters.agency_display: FinCEN (joint with OCC, Board, FDIC, NCUA)
letters.thesis: The account definition does two jobs in the GENIUS Act framework; the proposal codifies one and disclaims the other in a footnote that belongs in binding regulatory text.
letters.gaps: Gaps: a narrow codified account definition sits beside a codified lawful-order cross-reference with only footnote 57 between them; the population estimate counts on-chain counterparties while the obligation attaches to formal relationships; the government-list comparison obligation has no designated lists.
letters.card_meta: 2026-08-21 · FinCEN (joint with OCC, Board, FDIC, NCUA) · Control-layer + on-chain measurement · 8 recs

recommendations.ask: Codify the account-definition boundary
recommendations.text: Codify the account-definition boundary (Questions 2 and 3; proposed Sections 1033.100(a) and 1033.220(c)). Move the footnote 57 disclaimer into regulatory text, so the customer identification definition of account cannot be read into the lawful-order obligation that Section 1033.220(c) preserves. Carries forward the position already on the record at FINCEN-2026-0100 (wallet address as account for lawful orders) by citation rather than re-argument. The signature multi-docket contribution of a commenter present on both dockets.

recommendations.ask: Observable hallmarks of a formal relationship
recommendations.text: Observable hallmarks of a formal relationship (Questions 2 and 3; proposed Section 1033.100(a)(1)). Retain "formal relationship" but state its hallmarks as observable attributes, stated non-exclusively: a contractual right of redemption against the issuer, an onboarding record, membership on an authorized-participant or minter list, a custody agreement. Reconcile with the mutual fund CIP "contractual or other business relationship" formulation that the proposal's own footnote 59 flags. A relationship test that turns on the issuer's characterization of it is not examinable.

recommendations.ask: Conform the preamble to the codified account text
recommendations.text: Conform the preamble to the codified account text (Question 2; proposed Section 1033.100(a)(1)(v)). The preamble at 91 Fed. Reg. 37239 describes subparagraph (a)(1)(v) with three qualifiers; the codified text at 91 Fed. Reg. 37270 reads bare, "Providing services of a digital asset service provider." Resolve in favor of the codified text and correct the preamble: the qualified reading would relieve an issuer of customer identification duties precisely where its activities were unauthorized.

recommendations.ask: Redemption-only relationships
recommendations.text: Redemption-only relationships (Question 4; proposed Sections 1033.100(b)(2)(iv) and 1033.220(a)(2)(ii)). Confirm that a redemption-triggered account may be verified within a reasonable period after opening, so the rule does not operate as a gate on the one exit path that leads to par, with risk-based pre-completion verification preserved for unusual size or pattern.

recommendations.ask: The population estimate measures a different object than the rule reaches
recommendations.text: The population estimate measures a different object than the rule reaches (Additional Questions 1, 4, 8, and 9; Question 1). State which object the population estimate measures, and re-derive the affected-population and burden estimates on the account-holder object the rule defines. The program's strongest empirical fit to an explicit agency data request: the analysis counts on-chain counterparties, the obligation attaches to formal relationships, and the two have been measured separately.

recommendations.ask: Reliance asymmetry, and the threshold that determines which side an issuer sits on
recommendations.text: Reliance asymmetry, and the threshold that determines which side an issuer sits on (Question 7; Additional Questions 5 and 12; proposed Section 1033.220(a)(6)). Address the asymmetry the preamble itself identifies, under which a state qualified issuer may rely on a federally regulated PPSI but not the reverse, and reconcile the measurement basis of the ten-billion-dollar threshold that determines an issuer's position. The same numeral is now measured on a third basis (consolidated total outstanding issuance at 12 U.S.C. 5903(c)) against 10 billion dollars in assets at the OCC (AF55) and 10 billion dollars in outstanding issuance value at the FDIC (AG29).

recommendations.ask: Digital identity and verifiable credentials
recommendations.text: Digital identity and verifiable credentials (Questions 5, 6, and 8; proposed Section 1033.220(a)(2)(ii)). Do not name digital identity tools in regulatory text. State the four observable properties by which a credential supports a reasonable belief: the evidence and assurance level the credential issuer collected, the binding of the credential to the presenter, status and revocation checkability at the time of reliance, and how failures and indeterminate results are handled.

recommendations.ask: List comparison with no designated lists
recommendations.text: List comparison with no designated lists (Question 8; proposed Section 1033.220(a)(4)). The government-list comparison obligation currently has no designated lists. State the designation mechanism and the notification timing, and confirm whether existing OFAC sanctions screening discharges the obligation in whole, in part, or not at all. An obligation whose object does not yet exist cannot be examined for effectiveness, and cannot be costed.

letters.title: FDIC AG21 resolution submissions
letters.headline: FDIC AG21 resolution submissions comment
letters.h1: FDIC AG21 comment: keep the run-risk information the resolution rule would delete
letters.description: FDIC AG21 resolution submissions: keep the run-risk content the rule would delete; extend the receivership perimeter to tokenized deposits. Six recommendations.
letters.thesis: The rule narrows what covered institutions must submit for resolution planning, and the content it removes is disproportionately the content that predicts a run.
letters.gaps: Gaps: uninsured-deposit concentration and key-depositor detail, the variables March 2023 showed to be decisive, would be deleted while coverage is keyed to asset size alone; the receivership perimeter does not identify tokenized-deposit or stablecoin-reserve-custody arrangements or the operational controls at that boundary.
letters.card_meta: 2026-08-24 · FDIC · Run-risk measurement + control layer · 6 recs

recommendations.ask: A measured run-risk trigger, not size alone
recommendations.text: A measured run-risk trigger, not size alone (Questions 2 and 3; proposed Sections 360.10(b) and (c)). Do not de-scope the $50 billion to $100 billion cohort by asset size alone; key continued minimal coverage to a measured uninsured-deposit-concentration or rapid-growth trigger.

recommendations.ask: A retained uninsured-deposit-concentration element
recommendations.text: A retained uninsured-deposit-concentration element (Question 21). Retain a minimal uninsured-deposit-concentration and key-depositor data element rather than deleting it outright, at a fraction of the burden of the full submission.

recommendations.ask: Tokenized-deposit and reserve-custody linkages in the perimeter
recommendations.text: Tokenized-deposit and reserve-custody linkages in the perimeter (Questions 37 and 38; digital-services content). Require identification of tokenized-deposit and stablecoin-reserve-custody arrangements and the operational controls at the boundary, so a receiver knows what it can reach.

recommendations.ask: Current demonstration, not opt-in participation
recommendations.text: Current demonstration, not opt-in participation (Question 40). Key any reliance on the Resolution Readiness Adjustment to a demonstration that is still current, reconciling the assessments rule's credit with this rule's evidence.

recommendations.ask: A minimal public accountability signal
recommendations.text: A minimal public accountability signal (Question 44). Retain a minimal, calibrated public section or an equivalent accountability mechanism rather than removing public visibility entirely.

recommendations.ask: One operational-capability test, administered once
recommendations.text: One operational-capability test, administered once (Questions 16 and 17). Retain an operational-capability test that the covered institution can deliver the required output under test conditions, reusable as the assessments rule's Resolution Readiness Adjustment test rather than duplicated.

letters.title: FDIC AG27 assessments
letters.headline: FDIC AG27 assessments comment
letters.h1: FDIC AG27 comment: price the run risk the assessment framework is about to stop pricing
letters.description: FDIC AG27 assessments: price the run risk and novel-activity risk the framework is about to stop pricing. Four recommendations.
letters.thesis: The cohort the assessment rule reclassifies carries measurably higher run risk than the cohort it is priced against; the framework prices size and resolvability, not novel-activity exposure.
letters.gaps: Gaps: reclassified banks show higher uninsured and insured brokered deposit shares than the comparison cohort; no indicator reaches crypto-asset or stablecoin-reserve-custody exposure; a voluntary rate-incentivized readiness mechanism selects for the banks least likely to fail, so its loss-reduction rationale is weakest in the non-electing tail.

recommendations.ask: A run-risk factor for the reclassified cohort
recommendations.text: A run-risk factor for the reclassified cohort (Questions 1 and 2; the $10 billion to $30 billion threshold and Table 1). Retain a run-risk-sensitive factor for reclassified banks, or condition the reclassification on a measured uninsured-deposit-concentration or rapid-growth trigger.

recommendations.ask: A novel-activity and concentration risk indicator
recommendations.text: A novel-activity and concentration risk indicator (Question 12; Section IX). Add, or solicit comment on adding, a novel-activity and concentration risk indicator to the assessment framework, so the pricing reaches the exposure channel March 2023 demonstrated.

recommendations.ask: A Resolution Readiness Adjustment keyed to a current demonstration
recommendations.text: A Resolution Readiness Adjustment keyed to a current demonstration (Questions 13, 17, 18 and 25; proposed Section 327.18). Preserve the operational test the proposed text already defines, state the sufficiency standard, reconcile the seven-year data-access reengagement interval with the three-year retest, calibrate the adjustment jointly with the companion AG21 resolution proposal, and support observable partial credit.

recommendations.ask: Reserve-ratio slippage and the distribution of relief
recommendations.text: Reserve-ratio slippage and the distribution of relief (Question 12; material economic effects). Weigh the reductions' effect on the fund's recovery and their distribution against the fairness rationale, and state the reasoning: the roughly $4.0 billion per year reduction delays the fund reaching its 2 percent designated reserve ratio to 2035.

letters.title: Federal Reserve R-1835 AML and CFT programs
letters.short_title: Federal Reserve R-1835 AML and CFT programs
letters.headline: Federal Reserve R-1835 AML and CFT programs comment
letters.h1: Federal Reserve R-1835 comment: adopt the coordination provisions the sibling rules carry, and give content to the term the protection turns on
letters.description: Federal Reserve R-1835: adopt the FinCEN coordination provisions the sibling rules carry; define the term the protection turns on. Nine recommendations.
letters.agency_long: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
letters.thesis: Four agencies are writing one anti-money-laundering program rule four times, and the only substantive divergence in the Board's version is the coordination mechanism itself.
letters.gaps: Gaps: the Board's proposed Section 208.63 omits the two FinCEN consultation and information-sharing provisions the OCC, FDIC, and NCUA proposals carry, while the Board's Alternatives Considered section states that the proposal includes them.

recommendations.ask: Adopt the two FinCEN consultation and information-sharing provisions
recommendations.text: Adopt the two FinCEN consultation and information-sharing provisions (Question 23; new paragraphs in Section 208.63). The signature contribution. All three sibling rules contain them, at proposed 12 CFR 21.21(h) and (i) for the OCC, 326.8(h) and (i) for the FDIC, and 748.2(h) and (i) for the NCUA. This is the only substantive divergence between this rule and its siblings, and it is the coordination mechanism itself.

recommendations.ask: State the weighing factors for a significant or systemic failure, and retain the breadth of what the protection covers
recommendations.text: State the weighing factors for a significant or systemic failure, and retain the breadth of what the protection covers (Questions 6, 7, 21, 22, 24 and 26, and Question 5; Sections 208.63(a) and (g)). The second signature contribution, and deliberately two-directional. On the trigger: state the factors that bear on the judgment rather than a bright line, which would create the cliff effects the Board itself rejects in its Alternatives Considered section, drawing on the notice's own Section IV.C.2 examples, and answer Question 5's program-level versus component-level question because it governs the same trigger. The control-layer factor this program adds: a failure at a shared third-party dependency can be systemic in effect while presenting at any single institution as isolated. On the other half, the recommendation is contrarian and asks the Board to change nothing. The definition of a significant AML or CFT supervisory action describes what the institution is protected from, so narrowing it shrinks the shield; striking unsafe or unsound practices or conditions from it would let an action be recharacterized as a safety-and-soundness matter and escape paragraph (g) entirely. Breadth there is already bounded by the definition's conjunctive third element and its express examiner-observation carve-out. The American Bankers Association asked the sibling agencies for the same clarification of the trigger a month before this proposal published, and observed that uncertainty about eligibility means the protection will not benefit banks.

recommendations.ask: Answer the harmonious-function question by enumeration, not intent
recommendations.text: Answer the harmonious-function question by enumeration, not intent (Question 8). Enumerate each divergence between the Board's final rule and the FinCEN and Agencies final rules, and state the reconciliation for each, rather than stating an intention to align. The second half of Question 8 is answered from the notice's own footnote 40 statutory derivation, which contrasts 31 U.S.C. 5318(h)(1), where a program shall be established, with 12 U.S.C. 1818(s)(1), where it is established and maintained.

recommendations.ask: Key the effective date to the last of the four final rules
recommendations.text: Key the effective date to the last of the four final rules (Questions 28 and 29). Key it to the last of the four to issue, or state the interim compliance expectation, because an institution cannot sequence one program against four rules with independent effective dates. On Question 28 the letter declines formal size tailoring, agreeing with the Board's cliff-effect reasoning, while noting that a commensurate-with standard should scale to the risk presented rather than to asset size.

recommendations.ask: Reconcile the operative scope with the regulatory flexibility analysis, and state one small-entity figure
recommendations.text: Reconcile the operative scope with the regulatory flexibility analysis, and state one small-entity figure (regulatory flexibility analysis; Section 208.63). Two drafting paths are offered: a defined term in paragraph (a), or amending 211.5(m) and 211.24(j) in the same final rule. Separately, the analysis states the small-entity population two ways, approximately 439 at 91 Fed. Reg. 42379 and 464 in both cost computations at 42380. The arithmetic reconciles only with 464: 32 hours times 51.20 dollars times 464 entities is 760,217.6, printed as 760,218, and 8 times 51.20 times 464 is 190,054.4, printed as 190,054; at 439 entities the same arithmetic yields 719,257.6 and 179,814.4. The letter takes no position on which figure is correct and does not assert the estimate is materially wrong. It asks the final rule to state one number and use it in both places, which is responsive to the notice's own request that commenters describe the number of small entities affected.

recommendations.ask: Confirm that the rule's own distribution-channels definition reaches programmatic and control-layer arrangements
recommendations.text: Confirm that the rule's own distribution-channels definition reaches programmatic and control-layer arrangements (Questions 10, 11, 15 and 20; Sections 208.63(c)(1)(i)(A) and (C), and (e)). Confirm, rather than add a category: the Board already defines distribution channels as the methods and tools through which a bank opens accounts and provides products or services, including remote and other non-face-to-face means, and already names blockchain monitoring and analytics among encouraged innovative approaches. Confirm that the definition reaches tokenized and programmatic channels and third-party control-layer arrangements, and that a change in those arrangements can require a prompt risk-assessment update. On the Question 15 alternatives, retain promptly over a set schedule and significantly over materially, the latter because it would import a securities and accounting term of art. On Question 20(b), the same control-layer change that triggers a prompt update is the natural re-approval trigger, so the two questions should share one test rather than each carrying its own. The letter answers the objection that distribution channels is undefined and will evolve directly: the term is undefined in the codified text and defined only in the preamble, which is exactly why confirming it is the ask, and the evolution concern cuts toward under-inclusion rather than rigidity.

recommendations.ask: Anchor independent testing and the effectiveness determination in observable criteria
recommendations.text: Anchor independent testing and the effectiveness determination in observable criteria (Questions 1, 2 and 17; Section 208.63(c)(2)). Carry the notice's own objective-criteria language into the determination, along with its own statement that a program meeting the technical requirements on their face is not what the rule intends. On Question 2, frame the resource-allocation measure as coverage of identified risk rather than as input volume.

recommendations.ask: Treat banking a permitted payment stablecoin issuer as a distinct channel
recommendations.text: Treat banking a permitted payment stablecoin issuer as a distinct channel (Questions 9, 11 and 14). Confirm that a bank holding reserves for, or banking, a permitted payment stablecoin issuer evaluates that relationship as a distinct distribution channel, because the illicit-finance activity occurs among holders who are not the bank's customers and whose transactions never pass through the bank's systems.

recommendations.ask: Make the required accessibility run to authority and information, not location
recommendations.text: Make the required accessibility run to authority and information, not location (Question 18; Section 208.63(c)(3)). Clarify that the accessibility the rule requires of the designated officer runs to that officer's authority and access to information, not to physical location alone, where AML and CFT functions or control-layer operations sit offshore. This has particular force for the covered United States offices of foreign banks, which interacts with the scope recommendation above.

letters.title: CFTC 3038-0076 clearing organization requirements
letters.headline: CFTC 3038-0076 clearing organization requirements comment
letters.h1: CFTC 3038-0076 comment: define the evidentiary form of the tokenized-collateral equivalence determination
letters.description: CFTC 3038-0076: define the evidentiary form of the tokenized-collateral equivalence determination clearing organizations must show. Four recommendations.
letters.thesis: Clearing organizations must now show, instrument by instrument, that a tokenized asset conveys the traditional asset's rights, yet the Commission's collection captures that determination in no defined form.
letters.gaps: Gaps: a supervisor can see that a haircut was applied but not whether the instrument conveys the rights the haircut assumes; liquidation-path and redemption-path concentration analysis goes unrecorded; the determination carries no revisit date while haircuts are re-evaluated monthly.

recommendations.ask: Define the evidentiary form of the equivalence determination
recommendations.text: Define the evidentiary form of the equivalence determination (Regulations 39.13(g) and 39.27(b)). A defined record would capture the decision date, an instrument description sufficient to identify the tokenized collateral and its redemption or liquidation pathway, the framework applied, the outcome for each category, and the system-of-record reference. The five areas of regulatory concern Staff Letter 25-39 itself names would serve as a first set of categories, so the form needs no framework beyond what Commission staff have already published; the program's MVEP is offered as one more detailed model.

recommendations.ask: Record the liquidation-path analysis behind the 39.13(g) liquidity finding.
recommendations.text: Record the liquidation-path analysis behind the 39.13(g) liquidity finding. Tokenized collateral posts instantly and converts to cash through redemption paths that can constrict together. The record would capture the paths relied on, the stresses considered, and whether at least one path survives each, which is the analysis the regulation's stressed-conditions language and the unimpeded-liquidation requirement of 39.27(b)(4) already call for.

recommendations.ask: Record whether concentration was assessed at the redemption path, not only at the asset
recommendations.text: Record whether concentration was assessed at the redemption path, not only at the asset (Regulation 39.13(g)). A single categorical field. Concentration can sit beneath the asset, in the infrastructure through which it is redeemed: a National Bureau of Economic Research study found that the largest stablecoin issuer allowed six agents in an average month to redeem for cash, against 521 at a second large stablecoin, a difference no asset-level measure reveals.

recommendations.ask: Record when the equivalence determination was last revisited
recommendations.text: Record when the equivalence determination was last revisited (Regulation 39.13(g)). A date and an event class. Haircuts and concentration limits are already re-evaluated at least monthly under 39.13(g)(12) and (13); the determination they rest on has no comparable record, and the date makes staleness visible without the Commission having to set a review interval.

letters.title: FDIC AG30 disclosure of information
letters.headline: FDIC AG30 disclosure of information comment
letters.h1: FDIC AG30 comment: build the aggregated-analysis channel into the rule, with safeguards
letters.description: FDIC AG30 disclosure of information: a standing, safeguarded channel for aggregated analysis of supervisory data, open to researchers. Four recommendations.
letters.thesis: Supervisory material reaches the public by exception; a standing, safeguarded channel for aggregated analysis would let the supervisory process be examined before a failure, not after.
letters.gaps: Gaps: the channel appears only in the preamble, with no regulatory text, purpose, or safeguards; eligibility runs only to law firms and trade associations; a minimum count alone does not protect the largest institutions.

recommendations.ask: Codify the channel and open it to independent researchers
recommendations.text: Codify the channel and open it to independent researchers (Question 20; Section II.C.7.d). Adopt it as a new paragraph (f) of proposed Section 309.37 that states its purpose, eligibility, and safeguards, and make independent research organizations eligible alongside the law firms and trade associations the preamble names. The OCC's parallel proposal, whose comment period closed the same day, already gives a not-for-profit university or think-tank as an example recipient; consistent criteria across the agencies would let one research design operate under each agency's rule.

recommendations.ask: Keep institution-level data inside a controlled environment
recommendations.text: Keep institution-level data inside a controlled environment (Questions 20, 21, and 22). Release only aggregate outputs that pass review. In the simplest form, FDIC staff run approved analyses and release the results, the arrangement the statistical disclosure control literature calls remote execution. No recipient then receives another institution's data, which answers the re-identification risk and the competitor-information concern by design.

recommendations.ask: Protect the largest institutions, not only small cells
recommendations.text: Protect the largest institutions, not only small cells (Question 22). Require every released statistic to rest on a minimum number of institutions, limit the share any single institution may account for, and review combinations of releases. These are the threshold, dominance, and complementary-suppression rules the federal statistical system already applies to business data.

recommendations.ask: Require reproducible public disclosures
recommendations.text: Require reproducible public disclosures (Question 23). Any public disclosure based on the channel should state its method and parameters in enough detail for the FDIC to recompute it, and correct any figure the FDIC cannot reproduce. This checks computation, not conclusions, and does not reintroduce the preapproval the proposal removes.

letters.title: Treasury GENIUS (issuance, offer and sale)
letters.headline: Treasury GENIUS Act section 3 issuance, offer and sale comment
letters.h1: Treasury GENIUS Act section 3 comment: confirm on-chain that a foreign issuer's lawful-order capability exists, then reach the controls around it
letters.description: Letter to Treasury on GENIUS Act section 3: an on-chain check that a foreign issuer's lawful-order capability exists, and the controls around it. Seven recommendations.
letters.thesis: Of the two facts proposed Sec. 1523.3(c) turns on, a foreign issuer's technological capability to comply with a lawful order is readable from its deployed contract and on-chain history, while whether it will comply is not observable at all; the rule should name the observable check as a floor.
letters.gaps: Gaps: a capability check alone would clear an issuer whose controls around the capability are absent; the forward-looking limb has no stated evidence; the mandatory section 8 check misses the 30 days between a published determination and the trading prohibition; the authority to invoke the capability can sit with a party other than the signer.

recommendations.ask: On-chain capability check as a diligence floor
recommendations.text: On-chain capability check as a diligence floor (proposed Sec. 1523.3(c); Question 52). State, in the rule text or the adopting release, that reasonable due diligence on a foreign issuer's representation includes confirming from the deployed contract and its on-chain history that the represented capability to comply with a lawful order exists and that the authority to invoke it is identifiable, where the payment stablecoin is issued on a public ledger. A freeze or burn function either exists in the deployed code or it does not, and prior invocations are a matter of public record, so the check needs no cooperation from the issuer: an examination of the ledger, not an audit.

recommendations.ask: Diligence must reach the controls, not just the capability
recommendations.text: Diligence must reach the controls, not just the capability (proposed Sec. 1523.3(c); Question 52). Extend the expected diligence to who may invoke the function and under what internal authorization, whether limits exist on the privileged operations the same key can perform, and whether the issuer publishes a response commitment for a lawful order. A documented production overmint at a highly regulated issuer, whose freeze and mint capability scored high on the program's own index while a supply cap, a per-transaction limit and multisignature minting were absent, shows that a check of the capability alone would have cleared it; the comment states this as a limitation of the program's own instrument. The Act already pairs the capability with policies and procedures for permitted issuers.

recommendations.ask: Replace the unobservable "will comply" with an observable proxy
recommendations.text: Replace the unobservable "will comply" with an observable proxy (proposed Sec. 1523.3(c) and section 3(b)(2); Questions 52 and 53). Confirm that the forward-looking limb is satisfied by the issuer's documented history of responding to lawful orders and a published response commitment, plus a duty to re-check on defined triggers (a change in control arrangements or in the contract's privileged functions, a section 8 designation of an affiliated issuer, or a failure to respond to a known lawful order), with records retained; and retain the proposed "knows, has reason to know, or should know" standard over the no-reason-to-suspect alternative.

recommendations.ask: Key the mandatory section 8 check to a published determination
recommendations.text: Key the mandatory section 8 check to a published determination (proposed Sec. 1523.3(c); section 8, 12 U.S.C. 5907; Question 52). Under section 8(b) the trading prohibition takes effect 30 days after its Federal Register notification, so a check limited to a prohibition in effect can pass while the published record already shows noncompliance. Confirm that the mandatory element covers a published determination of noncompliance not since lifted, and state the designation list's current state, where a provider checks it, and whether Treasury will maintain a machine-readable source.

recommendations.ask: Retain reasonable belief, and name the observable evidence for it
recommendations.text: Retain reasonable belief, and name the observable evidence for it (proposed Sec. 1523.2(c) and Sec. 1523.3(e); Questions 38, 44, 62 and 64). Keep the reasonable-belief approach over the per se alternatives for both issuance and offers or sales, and name the categories of evidence that support it: deployed geographic-blocking controls and their coverage, sanctions and jurisdictional screening at onboarding, controls against location spoofing, and the handling of indeterminate results. The controls that establish location are themselves observable, so the standard loses nothing on verifiability.

recommendations.ask: Assess the capability where the invoking authority resides
recommendations.text: Assess the capability where the invoking authority resides (proposed Sec. 1523.3(c) and Sec. 1523.1; Question 52, see also Question 24). Confirm that the inquiry reaches the party that actually holds the authority to invoke the compliance function, including an affiliate, a foundation, a contract administrator or a multi-party arrangement, because a representation signed by an issuer whose key is held elsewhere describes a capability the signer does not control. No new obligation arises in the ordinary case in which the issuer holds its own keys.

recommendations.ask: Align the lawful-order test across the three rulemakings that carry it
recommendations.text: Align the lawful-order test across the three rulemakings that carry it (proposed Sec. 1523.3(c) and Sec. 1523.1(c); Question 4). State in the final rule's preamble how this capability standard relates to the lawful-order obligations in the FinCEN permitted payment stablecoin issuer rulemakings: whether an issuer that satisfies one satisfies the others, and whether a provider may rely on a determination made under them. On Question 4, align the definition of lawful order with FinCEN's, or state where and why the two differ.

letters.title: SEC Regulation Crypto Assets (second SEC comment)
letters.headline: SEC S7-2026-27 Regulation Crypto Assets comment
letters.h1: SEC Regulation Crypto Assets comment: an observable control condition for the Rule 400 safe harbor, not the issuer's representations alone
letters.description: SEC Regulation Crypto Assets (S7-2026-27): test the Rule 400 safe harbor against control read from on-chain state, not the issuer's word alone. Eight recommendations.
letters.thesis: Proposed Rule 400 conditions a permanent change in a crypto asset's status on facts measurable from public data but tests them only through the issuer's own certification; the more objective standard Question 131 asks about has at its core a definition of control the Commission has already written.
letters.gaps: Gaps: Rule 400 tests cessation only through the issuer's own certification about its own promises; it reaches only the issuer, not the affiliates and agents the 2026 Interpretation includes; its scope shrinks with what the issuer promised; it is one-way on its face; and no measurement methodology is specified for holder or voting data.

recommendations.ask: Add an observable control condition to Rule 400(a)
recommendations.text: Add an observable control condition to Rule 400(a) (proposed Rule 400(a); Questions 124, 127, 131 and 133). Both operative facts in Rule 400(a) as proposed are internal to the issuer: whether it has ceased the essential managerial efforts it represented or promised, and whether it intends to make new promises. Add a third condition, satisfied where neither the issuer nor any person acting for it holds a power to alter the associated crypto network or the subject crypto asset that can be exercised without holder approval and takes effect without a timelock during which holders may reject it. That is a yes-or-no fact the issuer already knows and a reviewer can check from the chain. The condition imports no market conception of decentralization: it tests one element of the Commission's own definition of a decentralized crypto system, operational control, in its narrowest, unilateral form.

recommendations.ask: Require the Form TR analysis and specify its minimum content
recommendations.text: Require the Form TR analysis and specify its minimum content (proposed Rule 400(b) and Form TR; Questions 128 and 130). Do not permit certification without analysis, since a certification with no reasoning attached cannot meet the Commission's stated purpose that "a reasonable investor could understand how the issuer made its determination." Specify three minimum elements: a privileged-function inventory of the admin keys, upgrade authorities, mint and freeze functions and equivalent capabilities, with the on-chain address or program identifier at which each resides and who controls each; where the issuer relies on governance dispersion, a governance-participation measurement with the methodology stated, including the address exclusions applied and whether delegated voting power was measured; and a related-person continuation statement on whether any related person is engaged in, or has undertaken to engage in, the efforts the issuer has ceased. Commissioner Peirce's 2021 Token Safe Harbor Proposal 2.0 asked more of its end-of-period exit report than proposed Rule 400 asks of Form TR.

recommendations.ask: Extend the Rule 400(a) condition to affiliates, agents and privileged-function holders
recommendations.text: Extend the Rule 400(a) condition to affiliates, agents and privileged-function holders (proposed Rule 400(a); Questions 125 and 127). Proposed Rule 400 addresses only "the issuer," so an issuer may cease its essential managerial efforts while a founder-controlled foundation, an affiliate or a development company under common control continues them, and the crypto asset still exits the definition of "security" permanently. The 2026 Interpretation that Rule 400 is intended to codify already reads "issuer" to include affiliates and agents of the issuer or a promoter. Extend the condition to those persons and to any other person who controls a privileged function in the Form TR inventory, but not to every Rule 100 related person: not to a consultant, a family member, a validator or a code publisher who is neither an affiliate nor an agent and controls no privileged function. The release's existing carve-out for post-functionality maintenance, which applies "whether by the issuer or another party," keeps ordinary maintenance outside the condition.

recommendations.ask: Specify the measurement methodology wherever holder or voting data is relied on
recommendations.text: Specify the measurement methodology wherever holder or voting data is relied on (Questions 28, 130, 131 and 132). The same crypto asset can be characterized as dispersed or concentrated depending on choices no rule currently constrains. In the program's fifty-two-protocol audit, excluding burn addresses and protocol-controlled addresses lowered measured concentration by a median factor of 2.3 times across the thirty-two protocols with complete logging, while delegation raised effective voting concentration above post-exclusion holdings in thirteen of eighteen protocols with sufficient governance data (2.5 to 25.6 times, median 4.4 times), with five exceptions where a mature delegate program dispersed voting below holdings. Independent work by Matthias Nadler and Fabian Schär reaches the same conclusion about holder data. Specify, in the rule text or the adopting release, that any holder-concentration measure excludes burn and protocol-controlled addresses and, where governance runs through delegation, reflects delegated voting power rather than token holdings alone. The comment offers the audit's documented corrected methodology and its executable replication package as one reproducible procedure.

recommendations.ask: Anchor the Rule 400(a) standard to network functionality
recommendations.text: Anchor the Rule 400(a) standard to network functionality (proposed Rule 400(a); Questions 131, 132 and 133). Rule 400(a) is scoped by the issuer's own representations, so an issuer that described an extensive development program must complete or abandon all of it, while one that described little has little to cease; that asymmetry runs against Rule 103's aim of fuller disclosure. Incorporate the functionality anchor the release already articulates as an independent element, so the condition turns on the state of the network as well as on the completion of what was promised, and define it in the Commission's terms rather than the issuer's, after the 2026 Interpretation's definition of a "functional" crypto system: one whose native crypto asset can be used on the system in accordance with its programmatic utility.

recommendations.ask: Condition continued reliance on non-resumption, with prompt notice if efforts resume
recommendations.text: Condition continued reliance on non-resumption, with prompt notice if efforts resume (proposed Rule 400, new paragraph (c); Questions 127 and 134). Rule 400 operates once, and its only forward-looking element is the statement that the issuer "does not intend to make" new representations or promises, which neither the Commission nor investors can observe. Condition continued reliance on the safe harbor on the issuer not resuming essential managerial efforts, and require prompt notice if it does, on the model of the Form 1-UC current report (the suggested rule text gives four business days). On Question 134, state that filing Form TR is not, by itself, an admission that the asset was subject to an investment contract; the filing remains subject to the antifraud provisions. The comment leaves open whether issuers will rely on the 2026 Interpretation instead of Rule 400, on which it has no evidence.

recommendations.ask: State Rule 103(b)(1) progress against the milestones the issuer disclosed
recommendations.text: State Rule 103(b)(1) progress against the milestones the issuer disclosed (proposed Rule 103(b)(1); Questions 26 through 30). Progress is measurable only against a stated baseline: if the initial disclosure describes undertakings in narrative terms without identifiable milestones, the Form TR completion analysis inherits the same indeterminacy. Require the issuer to identify the specific milestones or deliverables comprising its represented essential managerial efforts and to state progress against each. This is the one place the comment supports a prescriptive element, because the safe harbor later depends on it; otherwise it supports Rule 103's principles-based approach. The 2026 Interpretation already treats a business plan containing detailed milestones as the kind of representation that speaks directly to essential managerial efforts.

recommendations.ask: Align the control test with sibling agencies' effective-control standards
recommendations.text: Align the control test with sibling agencies' effective-control standards (adopting release; Questions 127 and 131). State in the adopting release that the Rule 400(a) determination looks to effective control rather than nominal arrangement, and that placing an effort with an affiliate or agent does not by itself establish cessation, the same diagnostic the program applied in its FinCEN (FINCEN-2026-0034, Recommendation 4) and FDIC (RIN 3064-AG29, Recommendation 5) comments. Divergent tests for who controls a network invite forum selection rather than compliance, and the Rule 400 line is becoming a boundary between two regimes: the CFTC's October 5, 2026 advance notice presents its framework as complementary to the safe harbor, so the Form TR record should rest on effective-control facts both agencies can read.

letters.title: SEC tokenized NMS stock exemptions (File No. 4-927)
letters.headline: SEC File No. 4-927 tokenized NMS stock exemptions comment
letters.h1: SEC File No. 4-927 comment: collect from day one the facts tokenized NMS stock rulemaking will need, in a form checkable against the public ledger
letters.description: Letter to the SEC on its tokenized NMS stock exemptions (File No. 4-927): collect the ledger facts rulemaking will need, in checkable form. Seven recommendations.

comment_period.note: open-ended request for comment; the Order sets no deadline

letters.thesis: Several of the Order's conditions turn on facts the public ledger already shows, but the Order collects them as descriptions of procedure, only for a venue's own contracts, or not at all; a five-year exemption meant to inform rulemaking should collect them from its first day, in a form checkable against the ledger.
letters.gaps: Gaps: the change-control disclosure reaches only the venue's own contracts, not the tokens in its pools; the same-rights test does not reach the holder's exposure to a failed third-party tokenizer; dollar prices omit the stablecoin conversion rate and the ledger transaction identifier; Notice item (y) names no legal point of finality for either leg of a trade.

recommendations.ask: Verify equivalence through the custody chain and the holder's position if the tokenizer fails
recommendations.text: Verify equivalence through the custody chain and the holder's position if the tokenizer fails (Section II.E; Notice items (h), (i) and (cc); Questions 1, 3 and 5). State that the Section II.E verification, and the Notice item (i) description of it, must address five things: the tokenization model; which record controls if the ledger and the off-chain record disagree, and how often token supply is reconciled to the shares held for holders; the holder's position if the tokenizer, custodian or any other intermediary fails; how corporate actions are applied to the token, and by whom; and who may convert the token into the share and back, and on what terms. The four rights the Order names run against the issuer, while the Commission's staff has identified a further exposure that none of them reaches, to the third party itself, "such as bankruptcy." Under item (cc), the TSV should name which of three approaches to corporate actions under around-the-clock trading it uses (halting trading during corporate-action processing windows, treating the ledger as the authoritative record, or synchronizing two records), when an ex-date adjustment takes effect on the token, and how a dispute about it is resolved.

recommendations.ask: Extend the change-control disclosure from the TSV's own contracts to every asset in its pools
recommendations.text: Extend the change-control disclosure from the TSV's own contracts to every asset in its pools (Section II.A; Notice items (h), (n) and (dd); Questions 1, 4 and 5). Add a Notice item listing, for each Tokenized NMS Stock and each paired asset, every function by which any person can mint, burn, freeze, block, force the transfer of, pause, restrict the transfer of, or upgrade or replace the code governing the asset; the address at which it resides; who can exercise it; and whether its exercise requires approval by more than one person or is subject to a delay, revised within five business days of any change. Treat an exercise as a significant operational event under Section II.I when it freezes, blocks, burns or forces the transfer of units held by a pool the TSV provides, or pauses transfers of an asset in that pool, or when the TSV or a Covered Firm supplying the pool holds the function, and confirm that "auditable" in Section II.A includes the authority to replace the audited code. Item (n) asks these questions only of the TSV's own applications, and the program's verification of four major tokenized Treasury products, as documented in March 2026, found no timelock in any administrative control chain.

recommendations.ask: State, for each leg of a trade, when the transfer is final and who bears the loss if it is reversed or frozen
recommendations.text: State, for each leg of a trade, when the transfer is final and who bears the loss if it is reversed or frozen (Notice item (y); Questions 4, 5 and 7). Require Notice item (y) to state, for each asset in a trading pair, the ledger event at which the TSV treats the transfer as final; the legal effect of that event under the terms governing the asset, including whether it transfers the security or security entitlement or instructs an off-chain record; and how loss is allocated if a completed transfer is reversed by a reorganization of the ledger or the asset is frozen after execution. Settlement is "near instantaneous" only if the ledger event is the legal transfer for both assets. Every fiat-backed stablecoin in the MVEP's sample failed its settlement-finality category for want of a finality analysis comparable to UCC Article 4A, and because a pool holds every liquidity provider's stablecoin at one contract address, a block on that address would freeze the stablecoin side of the whole pool.

recommendations.ask: Add the ledger transaction identifier and the U.S. dollar conversion rate to each transaction record
recommendations.text: Add the ledger transaction identifier and the U.S. dollar conversion rate to each transaction record (Section II.G; Questions 3 and 5). Add to the Section II.G minimum fields (vi) the identifier of the transaction on the distributed ledger and (vii), for any pair whose other asset is not denominated in U.S. dollars, the conversion rate used to state the price in dollars and the source of that rate; the TSV already holds both when it computes the dollar price. Without the rate, a reader cannot tell a move in the stock from a move in the stablecoin it traded against: in the March 2023 banking stress one stablecoin fell 10.4 percent below par on an hourly decentralized-exchange volume-weighted basis and 13 percent at the centralized-exchange intraday low, so the choice of conversion source alone moved the measured price by more than two and a half percentage points. Without the identifier, no reported print can be reconciled to the ledger.

recommendations.ask: Ask Covered Firms for their control over the parameters of pools they supply and their share of each pool's liquidity
recommendations.text: Ask Covered Firms for their control over the parameters of pools they supply and their share of each pool's liquidity (Section IV.A; Questions 8 and 10). Add to the Covered Firm notification, and to the records a Covered Firm must keep, any key, role or governance right held by the firm or its affiliates that can set or alter the parameters, fees, code or pause state of an AMM Liquidity Pool it supplies, together with its share of each such pool's liquidity at the end of each calendar month. The Order names control over pricing as the conduct that may make liquidity provision dealing, and on a ledger that control is exercised through acts the Order itself lists. A supplier that trades against a pool's price does not set it; one that also holds the pool's parameter, fee or pause controls is in a different position, and the two facts distinguish one from the other.

recommendations.ask: Determine affiliation for the volume and symbol limits by who can exercise a pool's privileged functions
recommendations.text: Determine affiliation for the volume and symbol limits by who can exercise a pool's privileged functions (Section II.F; Question 5). Confirm that control "by contract, or otherwise" in the Order's definition includes the ability to exercise the privileged functions described in Recommendation 2, so that, for the aggregation conditions, TSVs are affiliated where the same person, or persons acting together, can exercise those functions over an AMM Liquidity Pool that each provides. On a ledger the decisive power over a pool can sit with a shared key holder across entities that are not affiliated in the corporate sense, as with the single multisignature wallet the program found controlling several tokenized Treasury products. The reading adds no new category of affiliation and no disclosure beyond Recommendation 2, and it does not reach a shared software vendor, data provider or node operator that holds no such function.

recommendations.ask: Address the GENIUS Act's July 18, 2028 offer-and-sale restriction before it applies to a TSV's pairing of a payment stablecoin
recommendations.text: Address the GENIUS Act's July 18, 2028 offer-and-sale restriction before it applies to a TSV's pairing of a payment stablecoin (footnote 24; Question 4). With Treasury, state before July 18, 2028 how section 3(b)(1) of the GENIUS Act applies to a TSV's pairing of a payment stablecoin, and in the meantime require the Notice to identify, for each paired payment stablecoin, whether its issuer is a permitted payment stablecoin issuer. From that date, subject to exceptions, section 3(b)(1) makes it unlawful for a digital asset service provider to offer or sell a payment stablecoin to a person in the United States unless a permitted payment stablecoin issuer issued it. The date falls inside the Order's term, which runs to September 17, 2031, and footnote 24 leaves open whether a TSV is a digital asset service provider. The comment does not ask the Commission to limit paired assets by type.
